speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your symptoms better, can you tell me how old you are and if you've noticed any small red or purple spots on your skin? Also, have you had any recent injuries to your legs that might explain the severe pain?

text: 4-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing generalized fatigue and easy bruising for 3 weeks. Over the past week, she has developed a fever and severe leg pain that wakes her up at night.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any swollen or tender lymph nodes in your neck, armpits, or groin area? Additionally, has she experienced any weight loss, night sweats, or bone pain elsewhere besides her legs?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and easy bruising. I also have Fever, Severe leg pain that disturbs sleep.

text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 10.1 g/dL (low); Leukocyte Count: 63,000/mm3 (elevated); Platelet Count: 27,000/mm3 (decreased).

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood results show anemia, thrombocytopenia, and a very high white blood cell count, which strongly suggests acute leukemia. To determine the specific type, I need to see the morphology of the cells. REQUEST TEST: Peripheral_Blood_Smear

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Peripheral blood smear shows numerous immature cells (blasts) with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, fine chromatin, and prominent nucleoli.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of blasts confirms acute leukemia, but we need to distinguish between lymphoblastic and myeloblastic types. REQUEST TEST: Bone_Marrow_Aspiration_and_Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Findings: Predominantly immature cells that are positive for CD10, CD19, and TdT.

speaker: Doctor
text: The immunophenotype confirms B-cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia. DIAGNOSIS READY: B-cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
